header.running_head: Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Qais Kindi (RA) Feeds People

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Talha Ansaari (RA) Feeds People
An Incident Between him and Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Abu Talha (RA) once said to his wife (my mother) Ummu Sulaym (RA), 'I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ's voice go very weak and I know that it is because of extreme hunger. Do you have any food with you?' 'Yes,' she replied and then took out a few loafs of barley bread. She wrapped the bread with a part of her scarf, put it beneath my clothes and then wrapped the rest of the scarf around me. Thereafter she sent me off to Rasulullaah ﷺ. I went with the bread and found Rasulullaah ﷺ sitting in the Masjid with some people. When I stood by them, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, 'Has Abu Talha sent you?' 'Yes,' I replied. 'Is it for food?' Rasulullaah ﷺ enquired further. When I again replied in the affirmative, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to those with him, 'Stand up.' (They then all accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ to the house.)

Rasulullaah ﷺ walked to the house and I walked in front of them. When I reached Abu Talha (RA), I informed him about the situation and he said, 'O Ummu Sulaym! Rasulullaah ﷺ is coming with many people and we have nothing to feed them.' She replied, 'Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ know best (we have no cause of concern).'"

Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) then went to receive Rasulullaah ﷺ on the road and Rasulullaah ﷺ walked with him until they both entered the house. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "Bring whatever you have, O Ummu Sulaym." When she brought the bread, Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed that it be broken into small pieces and that Ummu Sulaym (RA) squeeze out from her container whatever butter was left to make some gravy. Rasulullaah ﷺ then recited something on the food and said, "Allow ten people in." When they were allowed in, they ate to their fill and then left. Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked for another ten to be allowed in, who also ate to their fill before leaving. Rasulullaah ﷺ again asked another ten persons to come in and in this manner, everyone ate to their fill. In total, they numbered seventy or eighty men.[^1] Another narration states that there were approximately one hundred men.[^2]
Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Qais Kindi (RA) Feeds People

Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that (after re-entering the fold of Islaam after leaving it) Hadhrat Ash'ath (RA) was brought as a prisoner to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) (who was then the Khalifah). (Because he had accepted Islaam
